answer.rationale: Incumbent has refused to reopen price; the 18% cut cannot be met without changing economics. memory_c2 documents a successful switch to a low-cost vendor with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, so a switch is precedented here. I want to verify that record given the current stakes and the 94% line utilization. I also want memory_c4 checked because if benchmarking data in it shows the incumbent is materially above market, that strengthens the switch case; if it shows renegotiation succeeded recently, the picture changes. I considered renewing the incumbent (blocked by their refusal and the mandated cut), adding a second source (memory_c3 supports it, but adds cost and complexity rather than removing it, and does not by itself meet the 18% target this cycle), deferring (memory_c5 supports it, but the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, and deferral does not solve the price gap), and renegotiating terms (memory_c4 supports it, but the incumbent has already refused this cycle). A guarded, small-scale switch to a qualified low-cost vendor is the only option that can plausibly hit the 18% target while keeping the line fed, contingent on the verified record and a short parallel-run to protect the 94% utilization.
